correctness.rationale: The two fixed-zero lattices and multiplier identities follow exactly by differentiating the defining map. Their equidistributed phase sequences imply the two-arcsine empirical multiplier law and exact sink density with zero boundary mass. A Cauchy bound plus density on the irrational torus line gives the exact increasing threshold. For increasing maps, the interval between any two adjacent half-integer fixed points is invariant and iterates are monotone, hence all orbits converge. The basin-width law follows by exhausting three possible basin-neighbor configurations; conditional uniformity of fractional jπ offsets within each repelling parity class is proved using irrational rotation mod 2. The two square-root coefficients follow from explicit arcsine expansions. The package checker passed for sampled derivatives, finite densities, cusp coefficients, monotonicity and the basin-mixture weights, but was not treated as a proof of any infinite limit.

value.rationale: The natural problem is to quantify the heterogeneous multistability observed in the motivating concrete map, not a chosen arbitrary parameter slice. An exact full basin-width probability law identifies the relative abundance of narrow, wide, and continuously distributed attraction regions throughout the entire globally convergent gain range. The exact multiplier-spectrum measure classifies all fixed-point sink densities at every positive gain and reveals two collective square-root phase transitions after folding first appears. These are mathematically interpretable structural invariants of the source model; higher-period dynamics and physical-basin weights are explicitly outside scope.
